title: Continuity of the stable influence polynomial
statement: Let $\\Omega$ and $I$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\\Omega$ indexed by $I$, with one distinguished index whose basis function is constant $1$, and whose basis functions are orthonormal for the inner product weighted by $\\pi$. For any natural number $n$, function $f:(\\Omega^n)\\to\\bbr$, and coordinate $i\\in\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, the stable influence polynomial in the real parameter $\\rho$ is continuous.
hypotheses_covered: $\\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\\Omega$
The indexed real-valued basis has a distinguished constant-one basis function
The basis is orthonormal for the $\\pi$-weighted inner product
$i$ is a coordinate among the $n$ coordinates
